title: Verifier-assisted evaluation of LLM-generated network configurations for deterministic reachability and isolation
research_question: When asked to translate high-level network intent into device-level configurations, how reliably do current LLMs produce configurations that satisfy deterministic operational properties (reachability, isolation, ACL policy compliance) as measured by a formal network verifier, and how much does an explicit generate–validate–repair pipeline improve that reliability?
confirmatory_hypotheses: LLM-generated configurations produced in a single-shot prompt will fail verifier-checked reachability/isolation properties on a substantial fraction (>20%) of tasks in the public synthetic topology/policy corpus.

A generate–validate–repair pipeline that uses a deterministic verifier to identify failures and requests targeted repairs from the LLM will significantly increase the fraction of verifier-passing configurations compared to single-shot generation (absolute increase >10 percentage points).
exploratory_questions: How much marginal utility (absolute pass-rate improvement) is obtained per repair iteration (up to three iterations)?
Which strata (topology size, policy class) show the largest/smallest repair success rates?
What is the median and distribution of model calls required per successful repair (cost-per-success)?
Do automated contamination-detection signals (n-gram overlap / exact-line matches) predict unusually high pass rates (possible leakage)?
benchmark_scope: Public synthetic topology/policy corpus (published alongside study artifacts) pairing realistic topologies, device templates, and intent→policy pairs (released with provenance).
Reference alignment to prior public evaluation corpora (NetConfEval-like public corpora) for scope comparison only.
primary_estimand: Per-task difference in verifier pass indicator (pipeline-after-up-to-1-repair) minus single-shot baseline pass indicator (paired proportion difference).
secondary_estimands: Per-iteration marginal increase in pass probability (iteration 1).
Median model calls per successful repair.
Stratum-specific pass rates (small/medium/large topologies; policy classes).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample: N=240 tasks drawn from the public synthetic corpus, stratified equally across three topology-size strata (80 tasks per stratum). Exploratory holdout set: 60 tasks (same strata distribution) reserved for exploratory analyses. Inclusion: tasks with well-formed intent→policy pairs and canonical device templates. Exclusion: tasks whose synthetic topology or device templates fail deterministic schema validation prior to prompting; such exclusions are deterministic and logged.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired difference in verifier pass probability (pipeline − baseline). Target effect: absolute increase of 0.10. Paired McNemar-style rationale: with alpha=0.05, power=0.80 and assumed discordant-pair sum ≈0.20, required n≈157; buffer and stratification lead to preregistered N=240. Will report achieved 95% CIs (exact/binomial or bootstrap), p-values, and observed minimum-detectable-effect conditional on observed discordant counts. Sensitivity analyses recompute power for observed discordance in [0.15,0.30].
exclusion_rules: Exclude tasks failing deterministic schema/format validation prior to prompting; exclusions logged with reason.
Exclude tasks with unresolved technical model/API failures after automated retry policy from the primary paired analysis (see missingness_plan); those are included in sensitivity analyses.
missingness_plan: Technical model/API failures: automatically retry up to 2 technical retries (total 3 attempts per call) with exponential backoff. If still failing, mark the task-call as 'technical failure' and exclude from the primary paired analysis (primary requires both baseline and pipeline endpoints available). Sensitivity analyses: treat missing baseline or pipeline outputs conservatively as verifier-fail in an ITT-style sensitivity analysis. All exclusions, counts, and reasons are deterministically logged and reported.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired binary outcome (baseline vs final-pipeline after up-to-1-repair) using McNemar's test (alpha=0.05, two-sided). Report absolute difference, 95% CI (exact binomial or nonparametric bootstrap), p-value, and effect size. Secondary: report per-stratum descriptive pass rates (80 per stratum). Exploratory analyses (iteration marginals, strata comparisons): label exploratory; when multiple secondary hypothesis tests are presented as confirmatory apply Bonferroni correction across those named secondary tests; otherwise report unadjusted p-values with explicit exploratory labeling. Provide model-call cost-per-success statistics (median, IQR). Include contamination-flagged vs non-flagged stratified reporting. Provide exact counts of discordant pairs and missingness, and sensitivity analyses treating missing as fails.
multiplicity_plan: One pre-registered primary outcome (paired verifier pass-rate difference). All other analyses are exploratory except pre-specified stratified descriptive reporting. If reporting multiple secondary hypothesis tests as confirmatory, apply Bonferroni correction across those named secondary tests; otherwise present them as exploratory with unadjusted p-values.
contamination_plan: Detection: automated exact-line matching (SHA256 per canonical config line), normalized 5-gram overlap scoring, and token-shingle Jaccard fingerprinting. Flags: 'possible-contamination' if exact-line matches ≥2 or normalized 5-gram overlap >0.30; 'likely-contamination' if exact-line matches ≥5 or normalized 5-gram overlap >0.60. Analysis treatment: report pass rates separately for flagged vs non-flagged tasks; primary confirmatory analysis will include all items but will present contamination-stratified sensitivity analyses and an alternate confirmatory analysis that excludes flagged items if pre-registered thresholds are crossed. Residual uncertainty: automated overlap detection may miss semantic memorization; sensitivity across thresholds will be reported.
stopping_rule: Per-task stopping: perform one baseline generation; if verifier passes, stop for that task; if verifier fails, perform at most one repair generation (maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1). Stop per-task after verifier pass or after exhausting the per-task model-call cap (1 baseline + 1 repair). Global stopping: complete all 240 confirmatory tasks or halt only for deterministic infrastructure failures logged and reported.
planned_outputs: Public synthetic topology/policy corpus and provenance metadata (released with study artifacts).
Repository with parser/canonicalizer/verifier code, unit tests, and canonical examples.
Full raw LLM outputs (baseline and repair), canonicalized configs, and verifier results per task.
Contamination-flag table, audit-sample logs, and line-hash indices.
Execution manifest (model id/version/time-stamps, per-call metadata, retries, errors).
Statistical-results file (counts, tests, CIs, p-values), failure-analysis record, and sensitivity analyses.
Evidence-to-claim table and nearest-work comparison matrix.
Complete IEEE LaTeX manuscript and BibTeX bibliography (five pages or fewer) and mandatory Disclosure Statement.
Compiled PDF (≤5 pages), autonomous revision log, and final-output hash manifest.
Concise NotebookLM presentation brief (machine-readable) for post-acceptance use.
